With the 2026 midterms fast approaching, we’re asking a simple question: What actually matters to voters right now?

In this midterm study guide, Vox’s Astead Herndon breaks down five forces shaping the election cycle. He examines the shifting foundations of both major parties—from Donald Trump’s rising unpopularity over inflation and foreign policy, to the ideological civil war within the Democratic base. Plus, Astead answers your questions about the growing influence of AIPAC funding, why "affordability" has become the central message for both parties, how data centers are triggering mass voter anxiety over the future of AI, and what Trump’s executive orders mean for the future of mail-in voting and election integrity.

America, Actually publishes video episodes every Saturday tackling key issues in politics, culture, and the economy. Subscribe to Vox’s YouTube channel to get them. Listen to episodes of America, Actually on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, or your favorite app.

If you enjoy our reporting and want to learn more, sign up for Astead’s weekly newsletter, Midterms, Actually. Just go to www.vox.com/midtermsactually to learn more, and get in-depth analysis about this year’s election right to your inbox.

In this episode, we talked about the concept of Vishnu and his various avatars, exploring how he is seen as the sustainer of the universe and the source of life. The hosts discuss the intricate details of Vishnu's avatars, highlighting the symbolism and the stories behind them. They also discuss the importance of sadhana and how it can help people connect with the divine.

This was an amazing episode about Lord Vishnu. I am sure that with this episode, we will gain a bit more understanding of Indian mythology and more. I hope you will enjoy this episode and let me know your thoughts in the comments section.

AIR 25 Bhavika Chopra shares a simple Sunday exercise that helped her build answer-writing fluency, conceptual clarity, and the ability to connect ideas across subjects.

Bhavika Chopra’s journey is a story of persistence and smart course correction. A graduate in Economics (Honours) from St. Stephen’s College, Delhi, she initially secured AIR 476 in UPSC CSE 2023 and was selected for the Indian Postal Service. Instead of settling, she chose to reattempt with a clearer strategy and stronger focus.

Hailing from Chandigarh and academically strong since school, Bhavika also worked at Ernst & Young before fully committing to UPSC preparation. Her transition from Economics to Sociology, combined with disciplined preparation, helped her secure AIR 25 in UPSC CSE 2025, making her journey both relatable and inspiring for aspirants.

Bhavika Chopra’s journey is a story of persistence and smart course correction. A graduate in Economics (Honours) from St. Stephen’s College, Delhi, she initially secured AIR 476 in UPSC CSE 2023 and was selected for the Indian Postal Service. Instead of settling, she chose to reattempt with a clearer strategy and stronger focus.

Hailing from Chandigarh and academically strong since school, Bhavika also worked at Ernst & Young before fully committing to UPSC preparation. Her transition from Economics to Sociology, combined with disciplined preparation, helped her secure AIR 25 in UPSC CSE 2025, making her journey both relatable and inspiring for aspirants.
